newsitem.title: USA: Solikamsk starts up magnesium granules venture.
newsitem.headline: Solikamsk starts up magnesium granules venture.

text.p: Solikamsk Magnesium Works of Russia said its desulphurization granules joint venture with Germany's ALMAMET GmbH started up last month with current output at full capacity of 2,000 tonnes per year.

The 50/50 joint venture, Solikamsk Zavod Desulfuratorov (SZD), is based at Solikamsk's magnesium plant in the Perm Region, the company said in a statement released through U.S. based International Magnesium Association.
Work is in progress to expand production to 6,000 to 8,000 tonnes of granules a year by the first half of next year if key Russian steel producers install desulphurization equipment.
"SZD is free to purchase magnesium elsewhere if price and other terms of purchasing are better than Solikamsk offers," the statement said.
Magnitogorsk and Nizhniy Tagil steelmills in Russia were expected to install the desulphurization injection technology needed to use magnesium granules for purifying steel during melting.
SZD said desulphurization will produce better quality steel for the oil and gas industries which have been hit by faulty steel pipes, and forced to import pipe.
Production of magnesium desulphurizing granules in the former Soviet Union has been limited, SZD said.
Some 200 to 240 tonnes a year were produced in Russia's Udmurtia Republic, with a similar amount at AVISMA, also in Russia.
Kalush in the Ukraine produces some 3,000 tonnes a year, SZD said, but this does not cover the latter country's demand.
"It was not a surprise that the first contracts of SZD were being concluded with Ukrainians under support of Ukrainian government," SZD said.
Swiss-based Minmet Financing Company, which has a stake in ALMAMET, bought a 15 percent share in Solikamsk Magnesium Works last year.

Solikamsk Magnesium Works forecast that magnesium for desulphurization in the Commonwealth of Independent States could reach 8,000 to 15,000 tonnes within five years, and 15,000 to 25,000 tonnes within ten years.
